source.text: וַיִּקְח֣וּ בְנֵֽי־אַ֠הֲרֹן נָדָ֨ב וַאֲבִיה֜וּא אִ֣ישׁ מַחְתָּת֗וֹ וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ בָהֵן֙ אֵ֔שׁ וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ עָלֶ֖יהָ קְטֹ֑רֶת וַיַּקְרִ֜בוּ לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֵ֣שׁ זָרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹ֦א צִוָּ֖ה אֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And took [the] sons of Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, each his censer, and put in them fire, and placed on it incense, and brought near before Yahweh strange fire which not he had commanded them.

en.L: And the sons of Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, took each his censer, and they put fire in them and placed incense on it, and they brought near before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} strange fire, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had not commanded them.
en.B: Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu each took his own censer. They put fire in it, laid incense on the fire, and offered before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} an improper fire, one {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had not commanded them to bring.
en.R: Nadab and Abihu, two of Aaron's sons, each took a pan for burning incense. They put fire in the pans and placed incense on top. Then they offered it before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. But it was the wrong kind of fire. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had not commanded them to bring it.

decisions.choice: strange fire: fire that was not permitted, outside what God had commanded
decisions.reason: The word describes what is outside, foreign or not allowed. It forbids "strange incense" on the incense altar (Exodus 30:9) and is used of someone who is not a priest coming near the sanctuary (Numbers 3:10, 38). The text does not say exactly what was wrong. It says only that God had not commanded it. The coals may not have come from the altar (compare 16:12), or the offering may have been made at a time or in a way God had not appointed.

decisions.choice: censer: a fire pan for carrying burning coals
decisions.reason: A censer was a shallow pan in which burning coals were carried and incense laid on them, so that its smoke rose before God (16:12-13; Numbers 16:6-7, 17-18).

decisions.choice: Nadab and Abihu: Aaron's two oldest sons
decisions.reason: They were Aaron's firstborn and second sons (Exodus 6:23). They had gone up the mountain with Moses and seen God (Exodus 24:1, 9-11), and they were ordained as priests with their father in chapter 8. Their death is remembered in 16:1; Numbers 3:4; 26:61.

decisions.choice: an improper fire (Balanced); the wrong kind of fire (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Strange" today suggests something odd. The point is that the fire was not permitted, so Balanced says "improper" and Readable "the wrong kind of". Literal keeps "strange fire".

decisions.choice: two of Aaron's sons; a pan for burning incense
decisions.reason: Aaron had four sons (Exodus 6:23), so Readable says "two of". It explains "censer" by what it was used for.

source.text: וַתֵּ֥צֵא אֵ֛שׁ מִלִּפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה וַתֹּ֣אכַל אוֹתָ֑ם וַיָּמֻ֖תוּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out fire from before Yahweh and consumed them, and they died before Yahweh.

en.L: And fire went out from before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and consumed them, and they died before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Then fire went out from before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and devoured them, and they died in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then fire came out from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and burned them up. They died there in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: fire went out from before Yahweh and consumed: the same words as 9:24
decisions.reason: In 9:24 fire went out from before Yahweh and consumed the offerings on the altar, and the people shouted for joy. Now the same fire consumes the two priests who brought what God had not commanded. The fire that showed God's acceptance also shows his holiness (verse 3).

decisions.choice: consumed: killed them by fire
decisions.reason: The verb means to eat up or devour, and here to kill by fire. The bodies were not reduced to ashes: in verse 5 they are carried out still in their tunics.

decisions.choice: devoured
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for eating. "Devoured" keeps the picture; Literal has "consumed" and Readable "burned them up".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֗ן הוּא֩ אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה׀לֵאמֹר֙ בִּקְרֹבַ֣י אֶקָּדֵ֔שׁ וְעַל־פְּנֵ֥י כָל־הָעָ֖ם אֶכָּבֵ֑ד וַיִּדֹּ֖ם אַהֲרֹֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to Aaron, it [is] what spoke Yahweh, saying, by those near me I will show myself holy, and before [the] face of all the people I will be glorified. And was silent Aaron.

en.L: And Moses said to Aaron, "This [is] what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke, saying, 'Among those near to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} I will show myself holy, and before all the people I will be glorified.'" And Aaron was silent.
en.B: Moses said to Aaron, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} meant when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, 'Through those who come near {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} I will show that I am holy, and in the sight of all the people I will show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory.'" And Aaron said nothing.
en.R: Moses said to Aaron, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was talking about when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, 'I will show that I am holy to those who come near {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory to all the people.'" Aaron did not say a word.

decisions.choice: among those near me I will show myself holy: God's holiness is shown in and through the priests
alternatives: among those near me I will be treated as holy
decisions.reason: "Those near" God are the priests who serve him (Exodus 19:22; Ezekiel 42:13). The verb means to show oneself holy or to be treated as holy. God is shown to be holy when those who come near him obey him, and, as here, when he judges those who do not treat him as holy (Numbers 20:12-13; Ezekiel 28:22).

decisions.choice: what Yahweh spoke: a saying not found word for word earlier
decisions.reason: No earlier passage has these exact words. The nearest are Exodus 19:22, where the priests who come near must keep themselves holy, and Exodus 29:43-44, where God says the tent will be made holy by his glory. Moses may be summing up such words, or quoting a saying not recorded elsewhere. The verb "I will be glorified" is the one used when God gains glory over Pharaoh (Exodus 14:4, 17-18).

decisions.choice: Aaron was silent: he did not protest or cry out
decisions.reason: Aaron makes no answer and no lament. His silence accepts what has happened, as the commands of verses 6-7 will require of him.

decisions.choice: show my glory
decisions.reason: The passive "I will be glorified" is put actively, God showing his glory, which is how he gains it (Exodus 14:4). Literal keeps the passive.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֣א מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֶל־מִֽישָׁאֵל֙ וְאֶ֣ל אֶלְצָפָ֔ן בְּנֵ֥י עֻזִּיאֵ֖ל דֹּ֣ד אַהֲרֹ֑ן וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם קִ֠רְב֞וּ שְׂא֤וּ אֶת־אֲחֵיכֶם֙ מֵאֵ֣ת פְּנֵי־הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ אֶל־מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And called Moses to Mishael and to Elzaphan, [the] sons of Uzziel, [the] uncle of Aaron, and said to them, come near, carry your brothers from before the holy place to outside the camp.

en.L: And Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, the uncle of Aaron, and said to them, "Come near, carry your brothers from before the holy place to outside the camp."
en.B: Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, who was Aaron's uncle. He told them, "Come forward and take your relatives from in front of the sanctuary, and carry them out of the camp."
en.R: Moses called for Mishael and Elzaphan. They were sons of Uzziel, Aaron's uncle. Moses said to them, "Come here. Carry the bodies of your relatives away from the front of the holy tent. Take them outside the camp."

decisions.choice: your brothers: your relatives
decisions.reason: Uzziel was a brother of Amram, Aaron's father (Exodus 6:18, 20, 22), so Mishael and Elzaphan were Aaron's cousins and close relatives of Nadab and Abihu. "Brothers" is used of kinsmen in this way (Genesis 13:8). They were Levites but not priests. Aaron and his remaining sons could not leave their service (verse 7), and a priest was not to make himself unclean by touching a dead body (21:1, 10-11).

decisions.choice: the holy place: the sanctuary, the tent and its court
decisions.reason: Here the word means the sanctuary in general. Nadab and Abihu died "before Yahweh" (verse 2), at the tent or in the court near the altar, and their bodies are carried from there out of the camp.

decisions.choice: the bodies of; the holy tent
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the men carried the bodies, and calls the sanctuary "the holy tent".

source.text: וַֽיִּקְרְב֗וּ וַיִּשָּׂאֻם֙ בְּכֻתֳּנֹתָ֔ם אֶל־מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר מֹשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they came near and carried them in their tunics to outside the camp, as had spoken Moses.

en.L: And they came near and carried them in their tunics to outside the camp, as Moses had spoken.
en.B: They came forward and carried them out of the camp in their own tunics, just as Moses had said.
en.R: So they came and carried the bodies outside the camp. The dead men were still dressed in their priests' tunics. The two men did just what Moses had said.

decisions.choice: their tunics: the dead priests' own tunics
decisions.reason: "Their" most likely refers to Nadab and Abihu, who were wearing the priests' tunics put on them at their ordination (8:13). The fire had killed them without burning up their clothes. The words could also refer to the tunics of the men who carried them, but the text says nothing of those.

decisions.choice: The dead men were still dressed in their priests' tunics
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear whose tunics are meant, as in the meaning decision.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֡ן וּלְאֶלְעָזָר֩ וּלְאִֽיתָמָ֨ר׀בָּנָ֜יו רָֽאשֵׁיכֶ֥ם אַל־תִּפְרָ֣עוּ׀וּבִגְדֵיכֶ֤ם לֹֽא־תִפְרֹ֨מוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א תָמֻ֔תוּ וְעַ֥ל כָּל־הָעֵדָ֖ה יִקְצֹ֑ף וַאֲחֵיכֶם֙ כָּל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יִבְכּוּ֙ אֶת־הַשְּׂרֵפָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר שָׂרַ֥ף יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to Aaron and to Eleazar and to Ithamar his sons, your heads do not let loose, and your garments not you must tear, and not you will die, and on all the congregation he will be angry; and your brothers, all the house of Israel, will weep [for] the burning which burned Yahweh.

en.L: And Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and to Ithamar, his sons, "Do not let [the hair of] your heads hang loose, and do not tear your garments, so that you do not die and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is not angry with all the congregation. But your brothers, the whole house of Israel, may weep for the burning that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has burned.
en.B: Then Moses said to Aaron and his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, "Do not let your hair hang loose or tear your clothes in mourning, or you will die, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be angry with the whole congregation. Your relatives, the whole house of Israel, may weep over the burning {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought about.
en.R: Then Moses said to Aaron and his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, "Do not show your grief by letting your hair hang loose or by tearing your clothes. If you do, you will die, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be angry with all the people. But your relatives, all the people of Israel, may cry over those {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned with fire.

decisions.choice: let the hair hang loose and tear the clothes: the usual signs of mourning
decisions.reason: Loosening the hair (or baring the head) and tearing one's clothes were signs of grief for the dead. The priest of highest rank was never to do them (21:10), and the person with a skin disease had to do them (13:45). Aaron and his sons are on duty in the sanctuary and may not mourn in this way.

decisions.choice: he will be angry with all the congregation: God, with the whole people
decisions.reason: The subject is God, though he is not named. If the priests broke his commands, his anger would fall on the whole people they serve, as a priest's sin brings guilt on the people (4:3).

decisions.choice: the burning that Yahweh has burned: the fire by which he struck them
decisions.reason: The people may mourn for Nadab and Abihu, though the priests on duty may not. "The burning" is the fire by which God killed them.

decisions.choice: in mourning (Balanced); show your grief by (Readable)
decisions.reason: The actions are signs of mourning, so Balanced and Readable say so. Readable names the LORD where the Hebrew has only "he", and says "all the people" for the congregation.

source.text: וּמִפֶּתַח֩ אֹ֨הֶל מוֹעֵ֜ד לֹ֤א תֵֽצְאוּ֙ פֶּן־תָּמֻ֔תוּ כִּי־שֶׁ֛מֶן מִשְׁחַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֖וּ כִּדְבַ֥ר מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And from [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting not you must go out, lest you die, for [the] oil of anointing of Yahweh [is] on you. And they did according to [the] word of Moses.

en.L: And from the entrance of the tent of meeting you must not go out, lest you die, for the anointing oil of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] on you." And they did according to the word of Moses.
en.B: Do not leave your place at the entrance of the tent of meeting, or you will die, because you bear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointing oil." They did as Moses said.
en.R: Do not leave the entrance of the meeting tent, or you will die. You have been anointed with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s oil." So they did what Moses said.

decisions.choice: the anointing oil of Yahweh is on you: you are set apart for his service
decisions.reason: Aaron and his sons were anointed at their ordination (8:12, 30). Being anointed, they belong to God's service, and it comes before the duties of mourning a family member. The priest of highest rank is likewise never to leave the sanctuary for the dead (21:10-12).

decisions.choice: go out: leave the sanctuary, to bury or mourn
decisions.reason: The command is not to leave the sanctuary to join the burial or the mourning. The tent's entrance is where they serve (8:33-35).

decisions.choice: your place at; you bear
decisions.reason: Balanced words the command as staying at one's post and the oil as something the priests carry on them.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Aaron, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Aaron, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Aaron. He said,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Aaron,

decisions.choice: Yahweh spoke to Aaron: to Aaron alone
decisions.reason: This is the only speech in Leviticus that God addresses to Aaron alone. Elsewhere he speaks to Moses, or to Moses and Aaron together (11:1; 13:1; 14:33; 15:1). He speaks to Aaron alone again in Numbers 18:1, 8, 20.

source.text: יַ֣יִן וְשֵׁכָ֞ר אַל־תֵּ֣שְׁתְּ׀אַתָּ֣ה׀וּבָנֶ֣יךָ אִתָּ֗ךְ בְּבֹאֲכֶ֛ם אֶל־אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד וְלֹ֣א תָמֻ֑תוּ חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Wine and strong drink do not drink, you and your sons with you, when you go into [the] tent of meeting, and not you will die, a statute forever for your generations,

en.L: "Wine and strong drink do not drink, you and your sons with you, when you go into the tent of meeting, so that you do not die; [it is] a statute forever for your generations,
en.B: "Whenever you or your sons go into the tent of meeting, you must drink no wine or beer, or you will die. This is a permanent rule for all your generations,
en.R: "You and your sons must not drink wine or beer when you go into the meeting tent. If you do, you will die. This is a rule for all time to come.

decisions.choice: wine and strong drink: wine and other fermented drink, such as beer
decisions.reason: The second word means an intoxicating drink other than wine, most likely beer made from grain. The pair often go together (Numbers 6:3; Proverbs 20:1). Isaiah 28:7 describes priests who stagger from them.

decisions.choice: a statute forever: a lasting rule, explained in verses 10-11
decisions.reason: For the phrase see 3:17. The text does not say that Nadab and Abihu had been drinking. The rule stands as a lasting safeguard, and verses 10-11 give its purpose: priests must judge clearly between holy and common, clean and unclean. Ezekiel 44:21 repeats it.

decisions.choice: a rule for all time to come
decisions.reason: Readable combines "a statute forever" and "for your generations" in one phrase.

source.text: וּֽלֲהַבְדִּ֔יל בֵּ֥ין הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ וּבֵ֣ין הַחֹ֑ל וּבֵ֥ין הַטָּמֵ֖א וּבֵ֥ין הַטָּהֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: and to separate between the holy and between the common, and between the unclean and between the clean,

en.L: and to separate between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean,
en.B: so that you can tell apart what is holy and what is common, what is unclean and what is clean,
en.R: You must be able to tell the difference between what is holy and what is not holy. You must also know what is unclean and what is clean.

decisions.choice: the holy and the common: what belongs to God and what is for ordinary use
decisions.reason: "Common" means ordinary, not set apart for God. It does not mean wicked. Holy and common is one pair; unclean and clean is another. Something common may be clean or unclean, but only what is clean may come near what is holy. See the note at 11:4 for clean and unclean.

decisions.choice: to separate: the priests' task of judging
decisions.reason: God himself "separated" light from darkness (Genesis 1:4). Now the priests must make such separations for Israel, and chapter 11 begins at once with clean and unclean animals (11:47). Ezekiel 22:26 condemns priests who failed to do this, and Ezekiel 44:23 restores the task.

decisions.choice: tell apart (Balanced); tell the difference (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb means to separate; here, to distinguish and decide. Literal keeps "separate".

source.text: וּלְהוֹרֹ֖ת אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֵ֚ת כָּל־הַ֣חֻקִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: and to teach [the] sons of Israel all the statutes which spoke Yahweh to them by [the] hand of Moses.

en.L: and to teach the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel all the statutes that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken to them by the hand of Moses."
en.B: and so that you can teach the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} all the rules {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given them through Moses."
en.R: You must teach the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} all the rules that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them through Moses."

decisions.choice: to teach: the priests are teachers of God's law
decisions.reason: Teaching Israel was part of the priest's work (Deuteronomy 33:10; Malachi 2:7). The laws of chapters 11-15 are the kind of rulings priests had to teach.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: The phrase means through Moses as God's messenger.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֗ן וְאֶ֣ל אֶ֠לְעָזָר וְאֶל־אִ֨יתָמָ֥ר׀בָּנָיו֮ הַנּֽוֹתָרִים֒ קְח֣וּ אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֗ה הַנּוֹתֶ֨רֶת֙ מֵאִשֵּׁ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְאִכְל֥וּהָ מַצּ֖וֹת אֵ֣צֶל הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ כִּ֛י קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֖ים הִֽוא׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Moses to Aaron and to Eleazar and to Ithamar, his sons who were left, take the grain offering which remains from [the] fire offerings of Yahweh and eat it unleavened beside the altar, for most holy of holy things [is] it.

en.L: And Moses spoke to Aaron and to Eleazar and to Ithamar, his remaining sons, "Take the grain offering that is left over from the offerings by fire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and eat it unleavened beside the altar, for it [is] a most holy [thing].
en.B: Moses said to Aaron and to his sons who were left, Eleazar and Ithamar, "Take the grain offering that remains from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s food offerings and eat it, made without yeast, beside the altar, because it is most holy.
en.R: Moses spoke to Aaron and his two sons who were still alive, Eleazar and Ithamar. He said, "Take the grain offering that is left from the food offerings burned on the fire for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Eat it beside the altar, made without yeast. It is very holy.

decisions.choice: the grain offering that remains: the people's grain offering of 9:17
decisions.reason: A handful of it had been burned on the altar (9:17). The rest belonged to the priests as a most holy portion, to be eaten without yeast in a holy place (2:3; 6:9). For the food offerings see 1:9, and for "most holy" see 2:3.

decisions.choice: remaining ... remains: the same word for the sons and the offering
decisions.reason: The two sons "who were left" alive and the grain offering "that remains" are described with the same verb. After the deaths of verse 2, Moses sees that the surviving priests still carry out the day's duties.

source.text: וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֤ם אֹתָהּ֙ בְּמָק֣וֹם קָדֹ֔שׁ כִּ֣י חָקְךָ֤ וְחָק־בָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ הִ֔וא מֵאִשֵּׁ֖י יְהוָ֑ה כִּי־כֵ֖ן צֻוֵּֽיתִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will eat it in a holy place, for your due and [the] due of your sons it [is] from [the] fire offerings of Yahweh, for so I have been commanded.

en.L: And you will eat it in a holy place, for it [is] your portion and your sons' portion from the offerings by fire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for so I have been commanded.
en.B: Eat it in a holy place, because it is the share set aside for you and your sons from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s food offerings. This is what I have been commanded.
en.R: Eat it in a holy place. It is the share that belongs to you and your sons from the food offerings burned on the fire for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This is the command I was given.

decisions.choice: your due: a fixed share assigned to you
decisions.reason: The word means an allotted portion, a share fixed by rule, as the Egyptian priests had their allotment (Genesis 47:22). It comes from the same root as "statute" (verse 9).

decisions.choice: a holy place: within the sanctuary court
decisions.reason: Most holy portions were eaten within the court of the tent of meeting (6:9).

source.text: וְאֵת֩ חֲזֵ֨ה הַתְּנוּפָ֜ה וְאֵ֣ת׀שׁ֣וֹק הַתְּרוּמָ֗ה תֹּֽאכְלוּ֙ בְּמָק֣וֹם טָה֔וֹר אַתָּ֕ה וּבָנֶ֥יךָ וּבְנֹתֶ֖יךָ אִתָּ֑ךְ כִּֽי־חָקְךָ֤ וְחָק־בָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ נִתְּנ֔וּ מִזִּבְחֵ֥י שַׁלְמֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution you will eat in a clean place, you and your sons and your daughters with you, for your due and [the] due of your children they have been given from [the] sacrifices of [the] peace offerings of [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution you will eat in a clean place, you and your sons and your daughters with you, for they have been given [as] your portion and your sons' portion from the sacrifices of peace offerings of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: But the breast of the wave offering and the thigh given as a contribution you may eat in any ceremonially clean place, you and your sons and daughters with you. They have been given to you and your children as your share from the peace offerings of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: But you and your sons and daughters may eat the breast that was waved before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the thigh that was set apart for the priest. Eat them in a place that is clean. These parts are your share and your children's share from the peace offerings of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: the wave offering and the contribution: portions given to the priests
decisions.reason: See 7:30-34. The breast was presented to God with a motion before the altar, the wave offering, and the right thigh was set apart for the priest as a contribution. Both came from the peace offerings (see 3:1).

decisions.choice: a clean place, with your daughters: less holy food for the priest's whole household
decisions.reason: These portions are holy but not most holy. The priest's family, daughters included, could eat them anywhere ritually clean (22:12-13). The most holy portions of verses 12-13 were for the male priests alone, and only in the sanctuary (6:11).

decisions.choice: the breast that was waved before the LORD; the thigh that was set apart for the priest
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two terms by what was done with each portion (7:30-32).

source.text: שׁ֣וֹק הַתְּרוּמָ֞ה וַחֲזֵ֣ה הַתְּנוּפָ֗ה עַ֣ל אִשֵּׁ֤י הַחֲלָבִים֙ יָבִ֔יאוּ לְהָנִ֥יף תְּנוּפָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְהָיָ֨ה לְךָ֜ וּלְבָנֶ֤יךָ אִתְּךָ֙ לְחָק־עוֹלָ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] thigh of the contribution and [the] breast of the wave offering, on [the] fire offerings of the fats they will bring, to wave [as] a wave offering before Yahweh, and it will be to you and to your sons with you as a due forever, as commanded Yahweh.

en.L: The thigh of the contribution and the breast of the wave offering they shall bring with the offerings by fire of the fat portions, to wave [them as] a wave offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and it shall be yours and your sons' with you as a portion forever, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded."
en.B: The thigh of the contribution and the breast of the wave offering are to be brought along with the fat portions for the food offerings, and waved before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a wave offering. They will belong to you and to your sons with you as your permanent share, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded."
en.R: The people must bring the thigh and the breast along with the fat that is burned as a food offering. Those parts are to be waved before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then they will belong to you and your sons. They are your share for all time. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded."

decisions.choice: they will bring on the food offerings of the fat: brought with the fat that is burned
decisions.reason: The worshipers bring the breast and thigh on top of the fat portions that will be burned on the altar (7:30). As in 8:26-27 and 9:20-21, the portions are waved before God and then given to the priests.

decisions.choice: a due forever: a permanent share
decisions.reason: The priests' right to these portions is lasting (7:34).

decisions.choice: The people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they will bring". Those who bring peace offerings are the worshipers, so Readable says "the people".

source.text: וְאֵ֣ת׀שְׂעִ֣יר הַֽחַטָּ֗את דָּרֹ֥שׁ דָּרַ֛שׁ מֹשֶׁ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֣ה שֹׂרָ֑ף וַ֠יִּקְצֹף עַל־אֶלְעָזָ֤ר וְעַל־אִֽיתָמָר֙ בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֔ן הַנּוֹתָרִ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And the goat of the sin offering diligently sought Moses, and look, it had been burned! And he was angry with Eleazar and with Ithamar, [the] sons of Aaron who were left, saying,

en.L: And the goat of the sin offering Moses diligently sought, and look, it had been burned! And he was angry with Eleazar and with Ithamar, the remaining sons of Aaron, saying,
en.B: Moses made a careful search for the goat of the sin offering, and it turned out that it had been burned. He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, the two sons of Aaron who were left, and he said,
en.R: Moses looked carefully for the goat that had been offered as a sin offering. But it had already been burned up! So he was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's two sons who were still alive. He said,

decisions.choice: the goat of the sin offering: the people's sin offering of 9:15
decisions.reason: Aaron had offered a goat as the sin offering for the people (9:3, 15). For the sin offering see 4:3. Aaron's own sin offering had rightly been burned outside the camp (9:11), but the people's was a different case (verse 18).

decisions.choice: diligently sought: searched with care
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. Moses looked into the matter thoroughly before he spoke.

source.text: מַדּ֗וּעַ לֹֽא־אֲכַלְתֶּ֤ם אֶת־הַֽחַטָּאת֙ בִּמְק֣וֹם הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ כִּ֛י קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֖ים הִ֑וא וְאֹתָ֣הּ׀נָתַ֣ן לָכֶ֗ם לָשֵׂאת֙ אֶת־עֲוֺ֣ן הָעֵדָ֔ה לְכַפֵּ֥ר עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Why not did you eat the sin offering in [the] place of the holiness? for most holy of holy things [is] it, and it he gave to you to bear [the] iniquity of the congregation, to make atonement for them before Yahweh.

en.L: "Why did you not eat the sin offering in the place of the sanctuary? For it [is] a most holy [thing], and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given it to you to bear the iniquity of the congregation, to make atonement for them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: "Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy area? It is most holy, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given it to you so that you may carry the guilt of the congregation and make atonement for them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: "Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy area? It is very holy. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave it to you so that you could take away the people's guilt. You were to make atonement for them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: to bear the iniquity of the congregation: the priests carry the people's guilt away
alternatives: the meat is the priests' share for making atonement
decisions.reason: To "bear iniquity" can mean to suffer for guilt, or, as here, to take it up and carry it away (Exodus 28:38; Numbers 18:1). Eating the sin offering was part of the priests' work of atonement. The text does not explain how the eating did this; it may simply mark the meat as the priests' due for the work.

decisions.choice: the place of the sanctuary; make atonement
decisions.reason: The most holy portions were to be eaten in the sanctuary court (6:19). For "make atonement" see 1:4.

decisions.choice: The LORD gave it to you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he gave"; Readable names the LORD so that the pronoun is not taken to mean Moses or Aaron.

source.text: הֵ֚ן לֹא־הוּבָ֣א אֶת־דָּמָ֔הּ אֶל־הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ פְּנִ֑ימָה אָכ֨וֹל תֹּאכְל֥וּ אֹתָ֛הּ בַּקֹּ֖דֶשׁ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוֵּֽיתִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, not was brought its blood into the holy place within; certainly you [should have] eaten it in the holy place, as I commanded.

en.L: Look, its blood was not brought into the holy place within. You should certainly have eaten it in the holy place, as I commanded."
en.B: Its blood was not brought inside the sanctuary, so you certainly should have eaten the goat in the holy area, as I commanded."
en.R: The goat's blood was not taken inside the holy tent. So you should have eaten the meat in the holy area, as I commanded."

decisions.choice: its blood was not brought inside: so its meat was for the priests
decisions.reason: When a sin offering's blood was brought into the tent to make atonement in the holy place, its meat was burned, not eaten (4:5-7, 16-21; 6:23). The people's goat had its blood put only on the altar of burnt offering outside (9:9, 15), so its meat should have been eaten by the priests.

decisions.choice: certainly you should have eaten it
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. In this setting it states what ought to have been done.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר אַהֲרֹ֜ן אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה הֵ֣ן הַ֠יּוֹם הִקְרִ֨יבוּ אֶת־חַטָּאתָ֤ם וְאֶת־עֹֽלָתָם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַתִּקְרֶ֥אנָה אֹתִ֖י כָּאֵ֑לֶּה וְאָכַ֤לְתִּי חַטָּאת֙ הַיּ֔וֹם הַיִּיטַ֖ב בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Aaron to Moses, look, today they presented their sin offering and their burnt offering before Yahweh, and happened to me [things] like these; and [if] I had eaten a sin offering today, would it have been good in [the] eyes of Yahweh?

en.L: And Aaron spoke to Moses, "Look, today they brought near their sin offering and their burnt offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and [things] like these have happened to me. And [if] I had eaten a sin offering today, would it have been good in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?"
en.B: Aaron answered Moses, "Look, this very day they brought their sin offering and their burnt offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and still such things have happened to me. Had I eaten sin offering today, would that have been right in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?"
en.R: Aaron answered Moses, "Today they brought their sin offering and their burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Even so, these terrible things have happened to me. If I had eaten the sin offering today, would {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} have been pleased?"

decisions.choice: they ... their: most likely Aaron's sons, who helped with the offerings
decisions.reason: "They" may be Aaron's sons, who brought him the blood (9:9, 12), or the people, whose offerings these were (9:15-16). Either way Aaron's point is that the day of the first offerings was also the day his sons died.

decisions.choice: would it have been good in Yahweh's eyes: eating holy food on such a day might not please God
decisions.reason: Aaron does not explain his reasoning fully. He seems to mean that after what had happened, he and his sons were not fit to eat most holy food that day, so it was safer to burn it than to eat it wrongly. Moses accepts the answer (verse 20).

decisions.choice: these terrible things; would the LORD have been pleased
decisions.reason: "Things like these" are the deaths of verses 1-2; Readable says "terrible". "Good in the eyes of" means "pleasing to".

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיִּיטַ֖ב בְּעֵינָֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And heard Moses, and it was good in his eyes.

en.L: And Moses heard, and it was good in his eyes.
en.B: When Moses heard this, it seemed right to him.
en.R: Moses heard Aaron's answer, and he accepted it.

decisions.choice: it was good in his eyes: Moses approved
decisions.reason: The phrase echoes Aaron's question in verse 19. Moses judges that Aaron acted rightly, and the matter ends there.
